target_symbols: AST node types for try/catch and throw
behavior_constraints: throw expr; evaluates expr and throws the resulting value, any value type allowed
try { } catch(e) { } runs try body; on throw inside (including nested calls), control jumps to catch with e bound to thrown value
if no throw occurs inside try body, catch block is skipped
throw must propagate across function call boundaries via stack unwinding: pop call frames until reaching frame with active try handler, restore stack pointer, jump to catch handler
nested try/catch must work, and a throw inside a catch block is caught by the next enclosing try
uncaught exceptions print 'uncaught exception: ' + value to stderr and exit with code 255
execution after try/catch continues normally when exception is caught
throwing inside a function called from within try must not leave the stack corrupted
affected_prior: vm_run (call/return control flow must cooperate with handler stack and unwinding)
compile_node (new statement nodes must be compiled; existing statement flow may need OP_POP_HANDLER on normal exit)
lexer_tokenize/lex_ident (new keywords must not clash with identifiers)
entities.summary: This round adds try/catch/throw exception handling with cross-function-call stack unwinding and uncaught-exception termination to stderr.

instruction_head:
Add exception handling with `try`/`catch`/`throw` and stack unwinding.

**`throw expr;`** evaluates `expr` and throws the resulting value as an exception. Any value type can be thrown (string, integer, array, hashmap).

**`try { ... } catch(e) { ... }`** executes the try body. If a `throw` occurs anywhere inside the try body (including inside functions called from the try body), control transfers to the catch block with variable `e` bound to the thrown value. If no exception is thrown, the catch
